text:
Alec: Quick sync — launching the 'ambassador' handoff for private deploy packaging. Need to lock network ownership boundaries, upgrade lanes, and launch criteria. 30m huddle today?
Marta: I can join. We need a hard split between 1.0 and 1.x commitments (installer scope, ip-preservation, airgap).
Dinesh: NetOps note — customers expect to own peering and route tables. We cannot assume they will accept automatic inbound peering changes; define managed vs customer responsibilities explicitly.
Sara: From field: top customers demand non-disruptive upgrades with preserved IPs. If upgrades force IP churn they'll stall. Also asking for a CLI-based offline install path.
Kevin: Engineering constraints: current bootstrap requires outgoing access to S3 + control plane. Airgapped/offline needs artifact bundles + local registries — doable but adds work.
Alec: Draft proposal: 1.0 = VPC-only mode (customer-managed peering, host agent), online-only installer, documented rollback and canary. 1.1 = bundled airgap installer, IP-preservation upgrade lane, staged upgrade tooling. Thoughts?
Marta: Concern: 1.0 must not break existing Dedicated customers. We need a migration lane with golden image compatibility and DB schema compatibility tests. Add this to CI gate.
Dinesh: Agreed. We should produce a "net-owner checklist" that enumerates firewall rules, required CIDR blocks, and where NAT should live. Redwood owns the checklist; customer owns infra changes.
Sara: Can we have an automated preflight that customers run to gate installs? Field will push for it.
Kevin: We can ship `redwoodctl preflight --target vpc` for basic checks. ETA: 3 sprints for core checks, ~5 sprints for deep IP-preserve validations and heuristics.
Alec: Proposed launch criteria (draft): (a) successful peering test with 3 pilot customers; (b) preflight pass on 90% of field installs in pilot; (c) documented rollback + clear SLA notes. Is that acceptable?
Sara: :thumbsup: Add customer comms template for pilots — I'll draft and share.
Marta: Technical acceptance: >=95% e2e upgrade test pass rate on upgrade lane and zero data-loss for KV-store migrations in integration runs.
Dinesh: Add fallback contingency: if peering fails, traffic should fall back to proxy via dedicated egress. Need a fallback policy doc and runbook.
Kevin: We can implement fallback proxy routing but that's +2 sprints for engineering + ops automation.
Alec: Prioritization suggestion: aim to ship minimal 1.0 by EOY; target 1.1 (airgap + IP-preserve) in Q1. If field demand accelerates we re-evaluate. Agree?
Marta: Agreed.
Sara: Sounds good — I'll start the pilot comms.
Dinesh: I'll draft the net-owner checklist and share for review.
Kevin: I'll scope the `redwoodctl` preflight and add a ticket for proxy fallback.
deploy-bot: Reminder — please create an RFC under /docs/deploy and ping eng-releases before week close.
Alec: Thanks all — I'll capture action items and spin up a short RFC.
